thread:
jordan (CS): Escalating ACME: PrivateLink endpoint is flapping after an ACM cert rotation. App gets intermittent 502s, logs show TLS cert name mismatch and backend connection resets. Opening here for routing + cert context.

customer-acme: We're seeing ~5-10% of requests fail for ~30m after rotation. New cert is in ACM, attached to NLB, but some connections still present old cert chain.

maya (eng-support): Thanks. First-cut: can you confirm the NLB is using the new cert and target group health checks are passing? Also any changes to route tables or proxy host header rewrite?

customer-acme: NLB shows cert ARN updated. Health checks mostly green, a few 502/504 traces. We don't rewrite Host header; we rely on SNI.

samira (netops): Could be a stale route/cache on their VPC endpoint or a PHZ split-horizon hit. Are they using interface endpoint with private DNS (enableDns) + Route53 PHZ?

jordan (CS): They enrolled PrivateLink with Private DNS. We suspect mixed DNS responses during rotation. Customer ran a curl with --resolve showing both old and new cert chains on different requests. Paste below.

customer-acme: ```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood-acme.internal/ -H 'Host: api.acme.example' --resolve 'api.redwood-acme.internal:443:10.1.2.5'
* Connected to api.redwood-acme.internal (10.1.2.5) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* Server certificate: CN=old-cert.acme.example
* SSL: certificate subject name 'old-cert.acme.example' does not match target host name 'api.acme.example'
* Closing connection 0

$ curl -v https://api.redwood-acme.internal/ -H 'Host: api.acme.example' --resolve 'api.redwood-acme.internal:443:10.1.2.6'
* Connected to api.redwood-acme.internal (10.1.2.6) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* Server certificate: CN=new-cert.acme.example
* 200 OK
```

maya (eng-support): Interesting — two different backend IPs returning different certs. 10.1.2.5 vs 10.1.2.6. That suggests either target group has mix of instances or NLB has multiple TLS listeners with different certs. Can you run: `aws elbv2 describe-listeners --load-balancer-arn <arn>` and `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn <tg-arn>` and paste outputs?

customer-acme: Output attached, but TG shows both instances healthy. Listener shows single HTTPS listener with certificate ARN pointing to new cert.

lucas (infra): Two possibilities: (1) stale TLS session cache/KV on NLB or on client (long-lived keepalives) hitting older node; (2) proxy or intermediate (firewall) doing TLS offload with an older cert. Also check if there are multiple NLBs (blue/green) and DNS/phz TTLs sending traffic to both.

samira (netops): If using VPCE with interface endpoints, ensure that the endpoint ENIs are in correct subnets and that route tables for those subnets don't send some AZs to a legacy NAT/proxy. Also confirm security group egress allows 443 to the NLB IPs.

jordan (CS): Customer provided traceroute and ENI mapping:

customer-acme: ```
$ traceroute -n api.redwood-acme.internal
1  10.0.1.1  0.3 ms  0.2 ms  0.3 ms
2  10.0.2.5  0.7 ms  0.6 ms  0.6 ms (ENI-a)
3  10.0.3.6  1.1 ms  1.0 ms  1.0 ms (ENI-b)
```

maya (eng-support): ENI-a vs ENI-b mapped to different AZs. What I want to check: are there any ALBs/NLBs fronting different subnets with outdated certs in the customer's account? Also confirm DNS resolver caching: `dig +short api.redwood-acme.internal` from inside multiple subnets.

customer-acme: Dig results: some subnets returned NLB A records for old-nlb.example.com (old IPs), others new-nlb.example.com. PHZ association might still include old hosted zone entry. TTL was 300.

samira (netops): That explains it — split-horizon/PHZ updates propagation. Steps to repro and mitigation: 1) Confirm PHZ records removed for old NLB across all associated VPCs. 2) Flush VPC resolver caches by replacing endpoint or toggling enableDns? (Note: toggling can be disruptive). 3) As short term, attach old cert to new NLB as a secondary cert to make both responses present and avoid mismatch.

maya (eng-support): Also check client-side keepalive timeout — if existing TLS sessions were established before rotation, clients might reuse TCP session with SNI set to previous handshake. NLB TLS termination should negotiate per connection but check connection draining settings.

jordan (CS): Customer asks for exact commands to find PHZ associations and delete record. Provided sample AWS steps below.

maya (eng-support): ```
# list hosted zones with name matching
aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name "redwood-acme.internal"
# list VPC associations
aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id <zone-id> --query "VPCs"
# delete the A record for old-nlb in the zone
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id <id> --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"DELETE","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood-acme.internal","Type":"A","TTL":300,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"10.2.2.5"}]}}]}'
```

lucas (infra): For quick mitigation, you can: (A) Attach old cert as secondary to NLB (if cert chain still valid); (B) add short-term redirect/302 on new host to force new connections; (C) increase connection draining target so old backends finish then deregister.

customer-acme: We'll: 1) check PHZ across VPCs, 2) attach old cert temporarily, 3) rotate again with zero-downtime plan. One question: do Redwood endpoints (ours) ever cache DNS results and return mixed records?

maya (eng-support): Our PrivateLink endpoints don't cache customer PHZ records; they resolve via VPC resolver — so mixed records come from customer's PHZ rollouts or from client TTL and cached connections. We can help validate by asking you to run repeated `dig +short` and `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername api.acme.example -showcerts` across AZs.

customer-acme: Will run the checks now and follow up. Thanks for the tactical steps.

oncall-bot: Incident created INC-2026-1348 for tracking, priority P2. Assigned to maya and samira.

jordan (CS): I'll keep this thread updated with their PHZ changes and results. If we still see mismatches after removal of old records, we'll schedule a joint window to rotate cert with traffic cutover. :thumbsup:
